headline: Rocky Mountain West Gateway and Alpine Lake Access
reservation: Rocky Mountain National Park entry requires a timed-entry reservation during peak months; check the official NPS site for the Kawuneeche Valley entrance. Campsites and boat rentals are separate systems. Always verify current park policies before departure.

days.title: Glacial Waters and Historic Boardwalks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Grand Lake Village

stops.name: Grand Lake Shoreline
stops.detail: Explore the deep sapphire waters by boat to see historic summer cabins only accessible by water.

stops.name: Grand Lake Historic Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk the wooden planks to experience the 19th-century western atmosphere and local shops.

days.driving: Local village walking; allow 15 mins for marina transfers
days.note: Morning water is typically calmest for small craft; afternoon winds are common.

days.title: Kawuneeche Valley Wilderness
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the RMNP West Entrance

stops.name: Adams Falls
stops.detail: A short hike leads to a powerful waterfall set within a narrow stone canyon.

stops.name: East Inlet Trail
stops.detail: Trek through massive meadows where moose are frequently spotted grazing in the willows.

days.driving: Allow 30 mins from town; conditions vary by park traffic
days.note: The West Side is generally less crowded than the Estes Park side but requires park entry permits.

days.title: High Tundra and Continental Divide

stops.name: Trail Ridge Road
stops.detail: Ascend above the tree line to 12,000 feet for panoramic views of the Rockies.

stops.name: Holzwarth Historic Site
stops.detail: Tour a 1920s trout ranch to learn about early alpine tourism and homesteading.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours for round-trip scenic driving with stops
days.note: Trail Ridge Road is seasonal; check NPS status for snow closures.

intel.title: Trailhead and Village Staging
intel.text: Village parking near the beach fills early in summer; utilize peripheral lots for longer stays. Trailhead lots in the Kawuneeche Valley have limited capacity.

intel.title: High Alpine Reception
intel.text: Signal is strong in Grand Lake village but non-existent inside the National Park and on Trail Ridge Road. Download offline maps for all hiking routes.

intel.title: Mountain Gateway Services
intel.text: Fuel is available in Grand Lake and Granby; there are no services once you enter the National Park. Ensure a full tank before heading up Trail Ridge Road.

intel.title: Wildlife and Weather Windows
intel.text: Dawn and dusk are best for moose sightings in the valley marshes. High altitude storms frequently arrive by 2 PM; plan to be below the tree line by then.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Restrictions
intel.text: Snow closes high-elevation passes from late autumn through late spring. Some town streets allow snowmobiles in winter; check local winter traffic rules.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at EGE or DEN; Denver offers the most supply options. Granby is the last major town for large-scale grocery needs before entering the lake area.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for paved roads, but high-altitude performance varies. Check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved forest service roads.
plan.goldenHour: Point Park offers a sunset view across the lake toward the Never Summer Range, subject to mountain cloud cover.
